structuredIncident.summary: The R3 exit carrier beam fell from a raised top backup roll balance assembly after hydraulic isolation and bleeding on October 14, 2024 (Turn 2). The incident occurred in an outage configuration where work rolls and backup rolls were removed. Evidence indicates the gravity load was not independently secured by a rated mechanical block or restraint; lockout records show blank fields for such controls. A handwritten turnover note regarding keeper inspection lacks verification chain of custody, while video review suggests off-center displacement cleared interference points before failure. Crane involvement is contradicted by logs and witness testimony.
structuredIncident.focalEvent: R3 exit carrier beam falls from yoke into mill pit
structuredIncident.actualImpact: Beam landed on sled/scaffold platform; no injuries reported at time of fall, but area red-flagged for investigation due to potential SIFp severity.
structuredIncident.potentialImpact: Falling object with ~8,500 lb weight capable of causing severe injury or fatality if personnel were present in the pit during subsequent operations.
structuredIncident.normalState: Top backup roll balance normally supported by hydraulic pressure and/or mechanical restraint when rolls are removed; system designed to prevent uncontrolled downward movement under gravity unless positively restrained.
structuredIncident.eventState: Hydraulic B-system isolated and bled (0 psi); top backup roll balance left in raised position without documented independent positive mechanical control. Keeper installed but sufficiency under off-center displacement conditions is unknown. Beam displaced relative to yoke, clearing interference points before falling.

facts: Incident occurred at Indiana Harbor Hot Rolling and Finishing - R3 Roughing Mill Stand on October 14, 2024 (Turn 2).
Work rolls and top/bottom backup rolls removed for outage work prior to event.
Top backup roll balance left isolated in raised position; B hydraulics shut off and bled before fall.
Carrier beam fell intact with keeper still installed on recovered assembly.
No gross damage or fracture observed post-event on yoke, link, or keeper pin.
Video review shows gradual downward movement of yoke over two hours preceding fall; beam did not move while wedged but rotated and dropped after stop cleared lifting point.
Witnesses saw lower end rotate/drop without observing crane hook, rigging, or person touching it.
Lockout verification record (R3-EV-005) shows blank field for mechanical block ID regarding gravity control; no independent verifier signature present.

answers.text: Answer: The partner investigation review reported that the raised assembly did not have adequate independent positive mechanical control. This supports an inadequate gravity-restraint finding, but does not establish the precise location or presence/absence of every possible block in the yoke pocket. Support: GTDE-05_task_loto_review.md, Review findings: gravity remained hazardous after hydraulic shutdown and the reported field condition did not provide adequate independent positive mechanical control. Source class: controlled benchmark derivative of partner investigation findings, not an original signed inspection record. Limit: The original signed field record, block inventory, installation photograph and rated support specification were not supplied. A blank block-ID field in the earlier synthetic lockout form establishes a documentation gap, not by itself proof that no block physically existed. No evidence supplied establishes that personnel knowingly relied on wedging as an approved support strategy.

answerFetches.answer: The R3 Outage Work Scope and Sequence (R3-EV-007) explicitly requires that after removing backup rolls, personnel must 'Confirm balance and associated components in approved supported state' before proceeding to isolate hydraulics. The Energy Control Plan (R3-EV-004) further specifies for the gravity-raised roll-balance: 'Lower to designated rest position or install rated mechanical blocking/restraint.' However, evidence does not definitively confirm whether a specific procedure document explicitly mandates an independent block/crib/pin *specifically* when hydraulics are bled and rolls removed (as opposed to just lowering), nor does it prove the exact wording of the 'approved supported state' requirement in the task-specific procedure. The LOTO record shows a blank field for mechanical control, indicating non-compliance with documentation requirements or an omission.

trace.summary: Evidence packet establishes that the top backup roll balance was left raised with hydraulics isolated and bled. The lockout record shows a blank field for mechanical restraint ID, indicating lack of documented independent positive control. Video review supports gradual yoke descent after beam displacement cleared interference points. Anonymous notes and hearsay (crane rumor) are unreliable due to lack of verification or contradiction by logs. A conflict exists between the anonymous keeper-check note and formal procedure requiring verified mechanical restraint; this must be resolved by physical inspection records which confirm keeper presence but not pre-event sufficiency under off-center load.

trace.summary: The focal event (beam fall) was caused by a combination of conditions: gravity load on an unrestrained raised balance, lack of inherent design stop allowing off-center displacement, and reliance on unverified barriers (wedging/keeper). Contributing factors include procedural gaps in requiring independent mechanical restraint when hydraulics are bled and failure to formally verify keeper installation. Root-cause candidates involve both equipment design limitations (lack of stop) and organizational failures (procedure non-compliance or gap regarding independent restraint requirements).

added: The R3 exit carrier beam fell from a raised top backup roll balance assembly after hydraulic isolation and bleeding on October 14, 2024 (Turn 2).
Work rolls and backup rolls had been removed prior to the event.
The top backup roll balance was left in a raised position after hydraulic isolation.
The B hydraulic system was shut off and bled (gauge read 0 psi).
The top backup roll balance remained in a raised position without an independent mechanical restraint or verified support condition after pressure removal.
The carrier beam was wedged against mill components before falling once relative movement cleared an interference point.
Witnesses observed visible rotation of the beam prior to impact but did not see a crane.
Operational logs show no commanded crane travel or lift tickets for R3 bay during the event interval.
The lockout verification record shows the mechanical block ID field blank for gravity control.
The yoke moved downward gradually over approximately two hours prior to the fall.
The keeper remained installed on the link assembly after recovery.
No gross fracture was observed on the yoke or carrier beam components.
A handwritten turnover note regarding keeper inspection exists but lacks author, time, or chain of custody.
The B hydraulic isolation valve was reported to have slow bleed-through.
The design of the system did not include a carrier-beam stop to prevent wedging on mill spreader/posts when backup rolls are absent.
Procedure requires confirmation of approved supported state for balance after roll removal.
Procedure/Plan requires lowering or installing rated mechanical blocking/restraint for gravity-raised balance.
Exact requirement for independent block/crib/pin specifically when hydraulics are bled and rolls removed is not explicitly confirmed in provided text.
